PRENATAL GENETIC TESTING REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Chorionic villi (uncultured)
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Reason for Referral: Increased screening risk
Additional Testing Requested: Haemoglobinopathy testing
Gestational Age: [redacted] weeks

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence-Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR) for rapid aneuploidy detection

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from uncultured chorionic villi. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers on chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. A minimum of four informative markers were analyzed for each chromosome. Peak area ratios were calculated for all heterozygous markers. Normal diallelic ratios range from 0.8 to 1.4. Triallelic patterns or skewed diallelic ratios (>1.8 or <0.65) indicate trisomy.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13:
D13S631: 1.05 (normal diallelic pattern)
D13S258: 1.12 (normal diallelic pattern)
D13S742: 0.98 (normal diallelic pattern)
D13S628: 1.03 (normal diallelic pattern)

Chromosome 18:
D18S391: 0.95 (normal diallelic pattern)
D18S390: 1.08 (normal diallelic pattern)
D18S535: 1.01 (normal diallelic pattern)
D18S386: 0.92 (normal diallelic pattern)

Chromosome 21:
D21S1435: 1.11 (normal diallelic pattern)
D21S1411: 0.89 (normal diallelic pattern)
D21S1412: 1.06 (normal diallelic pattern)
D21S1446: 0.97 (normal diallelic pattern)

SUMMARY RESULT
rsa(13,18,21)×2

No abnormality detected

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis is consistent with a normal chromosomal complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) was detected in this sample.

LIMITATIONS
This test is designed to detect whole chromosome aneuploidies of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21 only. It will not detect:
• Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
• Mosaicism below 20%
• Segmental chromosomal imbalances
• Aneuploidies of other chromosomes
• Single gene disorders
• Maternal cell contamination below detectable levels

This result applies only to the chromosomes tested and does not guarantee a chromosomally normal fetus.

RECOMMENDATIONS
Based on these results, no further chromosome analysis is needed on this sample for the indication provided. The haemoglobinopathy testing requested has been forwarded to the appropriate laboratory.

If ultrasound abnormalities are detected later in pregnancy, please contact the laboratory to discuss additional testing options.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
